I’ve got an early report tomorrow, a short layover, then a turn the next day, and I can already feel the airport food situation coming for me. The worst part is I can’t tell if I’m actually hungry or just tired and dehydrated, and then I end up grabbing whatever is fastest.

Could you give me a few realistic, “throw it in my tote” snack ideas that won’t get gross after a long day? I’m trying to be better about hydration too (my skin looks so dull in hotel lighting), but I don’t want to live in the crew room bathroom. And… maybe a simple way to wind down in a tiny hotel room when my brain is still on cabin mode? Nothing complicated—just something gentle.

Also, not to be dramatic, but the uniform fit thing has been messing with my head lately. I’m fine, I just… don’t want to feel like I’m bursting out of my waistband on a busy month. No judgment, please.

That sounds like a lot to juggle—your body and mind are navigating so many shifts at once. It’s completely understandable to feel scrambled.

For snacks that travel well: individual nut butter packets, whole grain crackers, dried fruit, or a sturdy granola bar. For hydration, consider an electrolyte packet you can add to water—it can help more than plain water without constant bathroom trips.

To wind down in a small space: try a 5-minute body scan (focus on relaxing each part slowly) or gentle stretching on a towel. Even sitting with your feet up and breathing slowly can signal your nervous system to shift gears.

About the uniform: feelings about fit can bring up a lot, especially under stress. If you’d like, we can talk about ways to care for your body with kindness right now—not to change it, but to soothe the stress it’s holding. Would that feel helpful?

And if that’s too much to ask, can you at least talk me down from the spiral in a way that doesn’t make me feel disgusting? I’m trying so hard to keep it together and still look put-together. No judgment. Please.
